newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates static, supply better.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates static, supply better.

text.p: Croatian money market rates remained firmer on Thursday despite more comfortable liquidity in the banking system following days of strains, dealers said.
"The situation finally changed today. There was a strong supply and we managed to square all of the 14.8 million kuna in new demand," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She said there were no buyers for an extra 35 million kuna on offer in the morning trade.
Interbank call money loans were made at 11 percent, unchanged from Wednesday. Term rates ranged from 15 percent for two-week funds and 18 for two-month deals.
One insurer charged 17 percent for fresh one-month funds.

Banks were said to be reluctant to cut prices just yet as slightly lower demand was not expected to last long. But for now, their accounts continued to swell thanks to a transfer of budget funds for mid-month salary payments to civil servants.
Bank balances topped 420 million kuna on Wednesday, compared to 358 million Tuesday and only 298 a day earlier.

Only one bank had a tiny overnight shortfall of 92,000 kuna and another sought just over 40 million kuna. Ovenight deals are struck at one point below the daily average. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
